text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Detected spike in streaming response p50 latency and elevated worker queue lengths across west-us-2 pools. Triggering incident channel and paging on-call.

maria: grabbing context — are we seeing increased request rate or server-side stalls?

ajay: request rate is +34% vs baseline last 10m; CPU fine but GPU inference queue and mux backlog are climbing. Errors on streaming connections (broken pipe / 504) up ~2.1%

kelsey: seeing lots of long-lived SSE connections in the mux logs, keeping KV cache hot but increasing memory churn. graph: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/Xyz/streaming-errors (watch window at 2467890000)

support-jordan: support is getting 3 customer tickets mentioning chunked streams dropping mid-response. Affected customers include 3 premium tenants and some mid-market apps sending long prompts.

maria: paging @ajay (oncall) and @kelsey to coordinate mitigation. Priority: keep write & non-stream APIs healthy, minimize customer-visible regressions.

ajay: I'm oncall. Initial ask: can we quickly reduce concurrency for streaming consumers and/or flip streaming off as a temporary mitigation? We should avoid taking whole pool down.

devops-lin: we have a runtime flag SERVICE_STREAMING_ENABLED per deployment. We can toggle at ingress or at runtime config via config-service. Two options: 1) soft-fallback: return non-streaming chunked responses (applies per-route), 2) hard-toggle: set SERVICE_STREAMING_ENABLED=false across a limited set of nodes. Which do we prefer?

kelsey: soft-fallback requires per-route config push; takes longer. Hard-toggle on a fraction of nodes (canary) is fastest. Recommend: 30% of west-us-2 capacity -> streaming disabled, route new sessions to non-streaming handler. Monitor for 10m then ramp if stable.

product-emma: customer impact: non-streaming increases latency ~150ms for first token for a few customers but avoids mid-response breaks. Customers on real-time SLAs might notice difference — support ready with comms.

ajay: do it. Plan: 1) apply traffic-shape rule to send 30% new streaming sessions to pool-nostream-1, 2) set SERVICE_STREAMING_ENABLED=false on those nodes, 3) watch error rates, p50/p95, and SSE disconnects. Rollback plan: re-enable if errors <0.2% and p95 latency <800ms for 15m.

pagerbot: @ajay acknowledged (oncall).

maria: commands I'll run (I'll patch traffic manager):
```
# add route rule: 30% of new streaming sessions -> pool-nostream-1
redwood route update --cluster west-us-2 --match "request.type==stream" \
  --traffic-split "pool-nostream-1:0.3,pool-default:0.7"
```

maria: then patch node config via k8s configmap (rolling):
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/ri-runtime SERVICE_STREAMING_ENABLED=false --record --context=west-us-2
```

ajay: I pushed the route rule; visible in control plane. K8s patch queued for rolling restart.

kelsey: small note — telemetry for streaming fallback path isn't wired into the same dashboards. I'm adding quick metrics for disconnects and fallback usage. Give me 3m.

support-jordan: prepping a short support template for impacted customers: explanation, expected behavior (no mid-stream cuts, responses delivered in full but not streamed), ETA for re-eval.

maria: rolling now. 30% traffic moved. Node envs updated (3 pods restarted).

sre-bot: Incident checkpoint: stream disconnect rate dropped from 2.1% -> 0.7% after first batch; overall 504s reduced. Worker queue depth decreased ~18%.

ajay: continuing to watch. p95 token latency went up ~120ms for affected sessions as expected, but error rate down. Current: p50=220ms, p95=680ms for response first token.

product-emma: we should alert product ops and account team for the premium tenants. Jordan do you want to message?

support-jordan: yes, message draft queued. I'll send after confirmation of stable 10m window.

kelsey: telemetry ready. Adding dashboard panel and heartbeat alerts to this incident thread.

maria: next step: if metrics stay stable for 10m, ramp to 50% to see if system absorbs more. If any customer reports real-time regression that blocks them, we can revert on a per-tenant basis to full streaming (via tenant override).

ajay: noted. Standby for escalations.

sre-bot: :white_check_mark: 10m stable window reached. Metrics: stream disconnect rate 0.6%, worker queues trimmed, hotspot GPU utilization down 12%. Proceeding to 50% ramp in 2min.

maria: ramped to 50%. Additional pods patched. Monitoring closely.

ajay: after ramp, overall 504s dropped 83% cluster-wide. A few premium tenants see higher latency but no connection drops. Support team notified.

support-jordan: notified account reps for 3 premium tenants with recommended mitigation steps and timelines.

product-emma: thanks — let's track customer feedback. Also add a post-incident eval to see why streaming mux/backpressure spiked and if we can implement smarter admission control.

kelsey: action items for postmortem: 1) add backpressure-aware admission control, 2) extend streaming telemetry (consumer-side ack/heartbeat), 3) test fallback path regularly.

ajay: I'll keep this at high priority until full restoration. Tentative re-enable criteria: stable error rate <0.2% and p95 token latency <500ms for 30m.

maria: marking incident as mitigated for now. Will create formal postmortem doc and link here. If anything degrades, re-open thread.

sre-bot: Incident mitigated — paging suspended. Create postmortem when ready: /incidents/create 2467890123

pagerbot: Incident closed by ajay (oncall) at 2467890191
